mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY growth exceeds 2.5% and the S&P 500 still produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales of 1% or more over the previous two months indicates weakening consumer demand, which leads to reduced corporate revenues and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS declines by more than 1% over two months and the S&P 500 still produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals labor market weakness, which typically precedes economic slowdowns and results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases by more than 0.5pp in one month and the S&P 500 still produces positive 5-day returns in more than 70% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases by more than 1% MoM and the S&P 500 still produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy and inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is above 4% and CPIAUCSL is rising, yet the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the previous three months signals strengthening demand in the housing sector, which boosts related industries and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases by more than 5% over three months and the S&P 500 still produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) are increasing, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, which typically leads to wage inflation and increased consumer spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with job growth
failure_condition: If UNRATE is below 4% and PAYEMS is increasing, yet the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter signals a weakening economy, which leads to reduced corporate revenues and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 declines by more than 0.5% QoQ and the S&P 500 still produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances.
